sections.title: Media — every setting
sections.summary: The screen's image or video block — its source, size, placement, rounding, and an optional fade overlay. This guide documents every setting of the Media block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Media section
sections.summary: The Media section adds an image or video that supports the screen's message: a product shot, a before/after, or a short explainer clip. On a paid landing page strong visuals build trust and lift conversion, but keep them relevant so they reinforce the headline instead of distracting from the choice or button the visitor needs to act on. It shows on choice screens and the wheel picker; headline screens set their image inside the Content section instead.

sections.title: Where it appears
sections.summary: Covered screen types: ListMultiPick, ListSinglePick, GridMultiPick, GridSinglePick, WheelPicker.

sections.title: How rounded the media is
sections.summary: Rounds the corners of the media block; 0 is sharp and higher values (up to 50) make them softer. A small radius around 8 to 16 gives a modern, polished look; match it to the rounding on your buttons and cards so the whole screen feels consistent. Leave it at 0 for full-bleed media that touches the screen edges.

sections.title: Show an image or video
sections.summary: Turns the image or video block on or off for this screen; off means no visual is shown. Turn it on to add a supporting visual, since on a paid landing page a relevant image or video builds trust and lifts conversion. When enabled, it starts with sensible styling from your design theme that you can fine-tune in the fields below.

sections.title: Color of the fade
sections.summary: Picks the color of the fade over the media. Use a dark color (usually black) behind light or white text, or a light color behind dark text; the fade goes from this color to fully transparent so the image still shows through. Match it to your background or brand color for a seamless look, and choose whichever direction gives your copy the strongest contrast.

sections.title: Fade over the media
sections.summary: Lays a soft, see-through fade (usually dark) over the media so any text or button on top stays readable against a busy image. Turn it on whenever you place a title, subtitle, or button over the media; without it, light areas of the image can wash out your copy. When enabled, you get controls below to set the fade's height and color.

sections.title: How far the fade extends
sections.summary: Controls how far the fade reaches across the media (0 to 100%). Match it to where your text or button sits: if the copy is near the bottom, a 30 to 50% fade from that edge usually gives enough contrast without darkening the whole image. Increase it if text is still hard to read, decrease it to show more of the image clearly.

sections.title: How tall the media is
sections.summary: Sets the media height as a share of the screen (0 to 100%), so it scales on every device; the default is 50%. Use a larger percentage for an immersive, image-led screen and a smaller one when you need room for the title, text, or button below; on a choice screen, keep it modest so the options stay visible without scrolling. Setting a value pins the media just below the header for a consistent layout.

sections.title: The image for this screen
sections.summary: Add this screen's image by uploading a file from your computer or pasting a direct image URL, then confirm it in the preview. Use a high-quality JPG or PNG that's on-message for the screen — uploads are optimized automatically for fast loading on every device. To replace it later, upload or paste a new source here.

sections.title: Image or video
sections.summary: Pick whether this screen shows an image or a video. Use an image for a fast, lightweight visual that loads instantly; use a video for short product demos or motion that holds attention (it can loop). Switching type clears the current media, so choose before you upload. Keep videos short and light so the page stays fast, since slow loads cost conversions on paid traffic.

sections.title: Space around the media
sections.summary: Adds empty space on the four sides of the media (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't flush against the screen edges or neighboring content. Leave it at the default for a full-width visual. Increase a side to inset the media and give it a framed look with breathing room, rather than edge-to-edge.

sections.title: How media fills its box
sections.summary: Controls how the media fills its box. Aspect Fit shows the whole thing without cropping (you may see empty bars), Aspect Fill covers the box completely but may crop edges, and Scale to Fill stretches it, which distorts photos, so avoid that. The positional options (Top, Bottom, Center, and so on) crop to fill while keeping that part in view. Aspect Fill is the usual pick for an edge-to-edge banner; use Aspect Fit when nothing should be cropped.

sections.title: Where the media starts on top
sections.summary: Sets where the media begins from the top of the screen. Screen Top runs it edge-to-edge to the very top (great for a full-bleed hero), Navigation Bar starts it just below the header, and Safe Area keeps it clear of phone notches and rounded corners. Pick Screen Top for an immersive banner, Safe Area when nothing should ever be clipped. This is locked if you set a media height percentage below, which positions it for you.

sections.title: Replay the video on a loop
sections.summary: When on, the video replays continuously; when off, it plays once and stops on the last frame. Only applies to video media. Turn looping on for short ambient background clips that hold attention; turn it off for a demo or explainer you want watched once, so it doesn't loop distractingly while the visitor reads.

sections.title: The video for this screen
sections.summary: Add a video by uploading a file or pasting a direct video URL. Keep it short (a few seconds, ideally under ~30s) and lightweight so the page loads fast — long or heavy videos hurt conversion on paid traffic. Uploads are converted automatically to play reliably across devices, and you can pair this with the loop option below to replay it continuously.

translations.en: Fade over the media

Lays a soft, see-through fade (usually dark) over the media so any text or button on top stays readable against a busy image. Turn it on whenever you place a title, subtitle, or button over the media; without it, light areas of the image can wash out your copy. When enabled, you get controls below to set the fade's height and color.

en.name: Where to find “Fade over the media” in the editor.

nodes.label: Fade overlay · How far the fade extends

translations.en: How far the fade extends

Controls how far the fade reaches across the media (0 to 100%). Match it to where your text or button sits: if the copy is near the bottom, a 30 to 50% fade from that edge usually gives enough contrast without darkening the whole image. Increase it if text is still hard to read, decrease it to show more of the image clearly.

en.name: Where to find “How far the fade extends” in the editor.

nodes.label: Fade overlay · Color of the fade

translations.en: Color of the fade

Picks the color of the fade over the media. Use a dark color (usually black) behind light or white text, or a light color behind dark text; the fade goes from this color to fully transparent so the image still shows through. Match it to your background or brand color for a seamless look, and choose whichever direction gives your copy the strongest contrast.

en.name: Where to find “Color of the fade” in the editor.

translations.en: Size, placement & rounding

nodes.label: Size, placement & rounding in the section

en.name: Where the Size, placement & rounding sits inside the open Media section.

translations.en: Inside the Media section, this is the Size, placement & rounding.

nodes.label: Size, placement & rounding · Where the media starts on top

translations.en: Where the media starts on top

Sets where the media begins from the top of the screen. Screen Top runs it edge-to-edge to the very top (great for a full-bleed hero), Navigation Bar starts it just below the header, and Safe Area keeps it clear of phone notches and rounded corners. Pick Screen Top for an immersive banner, Safe Area when nothing should ever be clipped. This is locked if you set a media height percentage below, which positions it for you.

nodes.label: Where the media starts on top

en.name: Where to find “Where the media starts on top” in the editor.

nodes.label: Size, placement & rounding · How media fills its box

translations.en: How media fills its box

Controls how the media fills its box. Aspect Fit shows the whole thing without cropping (you may see empty bars), Aspect Fill covers the box completely but may crop edges, and Scale to Fill stretches it, which distorts photos, so avoid that. The positional options (Top, Bottom, Center, and so on) crop to fill while keeping that part in view. Aspect Fill is the usual pick for an edge-to-edge banner; use Aspect Fit when nothing should be cropped.

en.name: Where to find “How media fills its box” in the editor.

nodes.label: Size, placement & rounding · How tall the media is

translations.en: How tall the media is

Sets the media height as a share of the screen (0 to 100%), so it scales on every device; the default is 50%. Use a larger percentage for an immersive, image-led screen and a smaller one when you need room for the title, text, or button below; on a choice screen, keep it modest so the options stay visible without scrolling. Setting a value pins the media just below the header for a consistent layout.

en.name: Where to find “How tall the media is” in the editor.

nodes.label: Size, placement & rounding · How rounded the media is

translations.en: How rounded the media is

Rounds the corners of the media block; 0 is sharp and higher values (up to 50) make them softer. A small radius around 8 to 16 gives a modern, polished look; match it to the rounding on your buttons and cards so the whole screen feels consistent. Leave it at 0 for full-bleed media that touches the screen edges.

en.name: Where to find “How rounded the media is” in the editor.

nodes.label: Size, placement & rounding · Space around the media

translations.en: Space around the media

Adds empty space on the four sides of the media (top, right, bottom, left) so it isn't flush against the screen edges or neighboring content. Leave it at the default for a full-width visual. Increase a side to inset the media and give it a framed look with breathing room, rather than edge-to-edge.

en.name: Where to find “Space around the media” in the editor.
